title: F4R: Failure-Driven Recognition, Reconstruction, Refinement, and Redeployment for Continual Robot Self-Improvement
abstract: arXiv:2609.35575v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The real-world performance of current vision-language-action models is fundamentally constrained by the limited coverage of expert demonstrations and their insufficient understanding of physical interactions. A common remedy is to collect additional real-world demonstrations of newly encountered failures. However, this process is costly, inefficient, potentially unsafe, and difficult to scale. To address this challenge, we propose Failure for Rising (F4R), a failure-driven real-to-sim-to-real closed-loop learning framework that converts real-world failures into targeted policy improvement. F4R first uses an agent to automatically identify and diagnose failures from rollouts. It reconstructs each failure as an interactive, object-centric table-top environment that preserves the task-relevant spatial and physical conditions. The policy is then refined through failure-conditioned sim-real co-training followed by targeted reinforce

translated_title: F4R：基于故障驱动的识别、重建、精炼与重新部署的持续机器人自我改进框架
translated_abstract: 当前视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型的现实世界表现从根本上受限于专家演示覆盖范围的有限以及其对物理交互理解的不足。一种常见的补救措施是针对新遇到的故障收集额外的现实世界演示。然而，这一过程成本高昂、效率低下、存在潜在安全风险且难以规模化。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了Failure for Rising（F4R），这是一个故障驱动的现实-仿真-现实闭环学习框架，能够将现实世界中的失败转化为针对性的策略改进。F4R首先利用智能体自动从策略执行轨迹中识别并诊断故障，然后将每个故障重建为交互式的、以物体为中心的桌面环境，同时保留与任务相关的空间和物理条件。随后，通过故障条件下的仿真-现实协同训练以及针对性的强化学习对策略进行精炼（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: F4R提出了一种故障驱动的现实-仿真-现实闭环学习框架，通过智能体自动识别与诊断机器人失败案例、在保留关键物理条件的仿真环境中重建故障、并进行故障条件下的仿真-现实协同训练，从而将现实失败高效转化为针对性的策略改进，实现机器人的持续自我提升。
en_tdlr: F4R proposes a failure-driven real-to-sim-to-real closed-loop learning framework that automatically identifies, diagnoses, and reconstructs robot failures in interactive simulation environments, then refines the policy through failure-conditioned sim-real co-training, converting costly real-world failures into targeted policy improvements for continual robot self-improvement.
